title: ‘Strategic change and grasping nettles’: where now for John Lewis as boss exits?

paragraphs.en: “Going up?” After a tough week for department stores it feels as if that sales aspiration is as dated as the singsong phrase in the opening credits of Are You Being Served? Simpsons of Piccadilly, which inspired the fictional Grace Brothers department store in which the 1970s TV sitcom was set, is long gone , and several of its modern equivalents are now fighting oblivion.
paragraphs.zh: “要上楼吗？”经历了百货商店艰难的一周后，这句销售用语似乎与《您需要服务吗？》（Are You Being Served?）片头中那句抑扬顿挫的台词一样过时。曾启发这部20世纪70年代电视情景喜剧中虚构的格雷斯兄弟（Grace Brothers）百货商店的皮卡迪利的辛普森百货（Simpsons of Piccadilly）早已不复存在，而它的几家现代同侪如今也在挣扎求生。

paragraphs.en: The boss of John Lewis, Peter Ruis, clearly decided it was time to exit the elevator this week, announcing his abrupt departure from the UK’s biggest department store chain in a surprise statement. Days later, Harvey Nichols, the luxury Knightsbridge store that was once a byword for 1990s chic, was bought out of administration for a knock-down price by the owner of Sports Direct, Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，约翰·刘易斯（John Lewis）的老板彼得·鲁伊斯（Peter Ruis）显然认定是时候“下电梯”了，他发表了一份出人意料的声明，宣布突然离开这家英国最大的百货连锁店。几天后，曾是20世纪90年代时尚代名词的骑士桥（Knightsbridge）奢侈品商店哈维·尼科尔斯（Harvey Nichols）被体育用品零售商Sports Direct的所有者、迈克·阿什利（Mike Ashley）的弗雷泽斯集团（Frasers Group）以极低价格从破产管理程序中收购。

paragraphs.en: It was only nine months ago that Ruis was talking about possible expansion of the 36-store chain and a burst of investment was seen to have revived sales. Since then, trading has been tough, not helped by blistering summer weather during which shops on hot high streets have lost out to online specialists, while the high cost of living has put spending on big-ticket items such as sofas and beds on hold.
paragraphs.zh: 仅仅九个月前，鲁伊斯还在谈论可能扩展这家拥有36家门店的连锁店，当时一轮投资被认为重振了销售。此后，经营一直艰难，灼热的夏季天气更是雪上加霜——酷热商业街上的实体店输给了线上专业零售商，而高昂的生活成本使消费者暂缓了沙发、床垫等大件商品的支出。

paragraphs.en: John Lewis said Ruis had decided to step down to “pursue new projects”. Ruis said he was leaving with the business on a “stronger footing”.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·刘易斯表示，鲁伊斯决定卸任是为了“追求新的事业”。鲁伊斯则表示，他离开时公司正处于“更稳固的基础上”。

paragraphs.en: Insiders suggest he had been discussing an exit for months. However, this was greeted with scepticism by those who know the company well, given that John Lewis recently organised a media briefing led by Ruis on 3 September, just three days before he is due to step down. It is understood he will still hold the briefing, days before the group announces half-year results.
paragraphs.zh: 知情人士暗示，他几个月来一直在讨论离职事宜。然而，熟悉该公司的人对此持怀疑态度，因为约翰·刘易斯近日安排鲁伊斯于9月3日主持一场媒体发布会，而那时距离他卸任仅有三天。据了解，他仍将主持这场发布会，几天后该集团将公布上半年业绩。

paragraphs.en: Ruis is to be replaced by Will Kernan, a non-executive board member of the employee-owned John Lewis Partnership, which also runs the Waitrose supermarket chain. Those close to Ruis suggest he was leaving “on his own terms”, may have personal reasons for moving on, and did not appear to have a new job lined up.
paragraphs.zh: 接替鲁伊斯的是威尔·克南（Will Kernan），他是员工持股的约翰·刘易斯合伙公司（John Lewis Partnership）的非执行董事，该公司还运营维特罗斯（Waitrose）超市连锁。接近鲁伊斯的人士暗示，他是“按照自己的意愿”离开的，可能出于个人原因而另谋出路，似乎也并未安排好新工作。

paragraphs.en: Sources close to John Lewis who have worked with Ruis, a fashion veteran, say he and Jason Tarry, the chair of the department store’s parent group, have notably different career backgrounds and management styles, and were always unlikely to gel. Ruis returned to the business in 2024 after a decade away running retailers including Jigsaw and Anthropologie, while Tarry, a former Tesco executive, took the top job shortly after.
paragraphs.zh: 与这位时尚界资深人士鲁伊斯共事过的约翰·刘易斯内部消息人士表示，他和百货商店母公司集团董事长杰森·塔里（Jason Tarry）的职业背景和管理风格明显不同，始终不太可能合得来。鲁伊斯在离开公司十年、经营过Jigsaw和Anthropologie等零售商后，于2024年重返公司；而曾任特易购（Tesco）高管的塔里则在不久后出任董事长一职。

paragraphs.en: “I am surprised Peter has lasted as long as he has,” one source said. However, Tarry said Ruis had done a “fantastic job”.
paragraphs.zh: “我很惊讶彼得居然待了这么久，”一位消息人士说。不过，塔里表示鲁伊斯做得“非常出色”。
